title: GlyphSdf embossed: zero-width sliver walls out of glyph outlines (degenerate piece in the packed glyph outline stream)
body: Found by opus-rt6 (R892.8 speckle). Embossed GlyphSdf captures (latin-embossed 4, qps-rtl-embossed 7 strict-detector speckles) show isolated pixels in the glyph top-band colour (~154) or wall band (~96) on the plaque near letters. They persist with shadows disabled (probe D) and vanish with the glyph rows removed (probe P). At 2x (3840x2160) each becomes a dotted line continuing a thin bright sliver out of a letter: a zero-thickness extruded wall that rays hit only where they land within the hit epsilon. The walk treats every segment independently (it ignores ContourStart, which is harmless), so the likely source is a degenerate back-and-forth or zero-area piece in the packed outline stream (text shaping / glyph row builder / SetGlyphOutlineInstances). Evidence: ws ~/codeman-cases/undertow/reports/opus-rt6-evidence/speckle/sheets/zoom-2x/, run dirs C:\vixen-native\rt6-scratch\sp9-*, sp10-*. Next step: CPU walk of the latin row stream around the sliver to name the segment. Tier sol: root cause needs measurement across text shaping and packing.

title: Look-dev: isolated dark/lit dots on curved surfaces and outline bands (primary/shading path)
body: Found by opus-rt6 (R892.8 speckle). Strict speckle detector (ws opus-rt6-evidence/speckle/speckle.py: pixel differs from all 8 neighbours by >12 levels in one direction, and the 8 neighbours plus the 5x5 ring agree within 12) finds isolated dots in look-dev: late-afternoon angle 1 (2), angle 3 (5), night-service 1/2 (1 each), overcast 3 (1), plus GlyphSdf analytic-vs-voxel-*-yaw30 (1 each) and isolation-StoredNormals (1). For late-afternoon 3 all five persist with shadows disabled (probe D), and neither a larger gradient tap (h 1e-3 to 4e-3, probe N1) nor 12-step bracket refinement (probe N2) removes them. They sit on the yellow figure and on silhouette outline bands, so the cause is in the primary hit or shading path, not shadows. Coordinates in the report opus-rt6.md section 1b. Tier sol: cause not isolated.

title: GPU system generator: a callable in a hoisted leading guard is emitted with its block argument unindexed
body: Found by opus-rt6 (GB1 scatter). Kernel GPU-system generator. A [KernelSystem] body whose first statement is 'if (i >= view[0].instanceCount * TileBinOps.ScatterLanes(view[0])) return;' is hoisted into main() as 'if (int(linearId) >= view.values[0].instanceCount * ScatterLanes(view)) return;': the field access is rewritten to view.values[0] but the callable argument stays the block name, which does not compile. Workaround in VIXEN TileBinningSystem.cs: compute the callable into a local before the guard (the guard is then not hoisted). Fix in the kernel: apply the singleton-array rewrite to callable arguments in the hoisted guard, with a CodegenTool test beside ScatterShader_AppendsThroughAtomicCountsAndClassifiesWithASwitch. Tier luna: one emitter rewrite with an obvious test.

title: Cold pipeline-compile timings are masked by the AMD driver shader cache
body: Found by opus-rt6 (11-17). The same binary and shaders, each run with fresh private VIXEN_CACHE_DIR and SHARED_CACHE_DIR, compiled the RTL pipelines in 67 s and then in 5 s, 14 s apart (cc-stock-again, cc-stock-again2). The AMD driver keeps its own on-disk shader cache keyed by SPIR-V outside the VIXEN cache dirs, and other lanes evict it. A 4.7 s vs 65 s comparison was read as a vx10 compile regression. A cold-compile witness needs the driver cache disabled or keyed fresh, and the boot probe line should report whether the driver cache was hit (VK_EXT_pipeline_creation_feedback gives per-pipeline cache hits).
